title_en: Bank of China (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. v. Hongye Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over guarantee contract
keywords_en: civil; dispute over guarantee contract; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; legal person; financial institution; Contract Law; avoidance of mandatory rules in the application of law to foreign-related contracts; validity of foreign guarantee contracts without approval/registration; liability after invalidity of guarantee contract; partially upheld; foreign guarantee; irrevocable guarantee agreement; credit facility by Hong Kong bank; contract dispute; guarantee; dispute over guarantee contract against Hongye Company et al.
full_text_en:
Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited v. Hongye Company et al.

— Dispute over Guarantee Contract

Ruling Summary

1. Where the parties to a foreign-related contract choose the law applicable to the settlement of contractual disputes, and such choice circumvents the mandatory or prohibitory legal norms of China, the agreement on the choice of law shall have no legal effect.

2. If a foreign guarantee contract fails to undergo the procedures of approval and registration with the administrative authority as prescribed, the contract shall be determined to be invalid in accordance with law. Where both the main creditor and the guarantor are at fault for the invalidity of the contract, they shall each bear their respective corresponding liabilities.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2002) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 6

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shantou Hongye (Group) Co., Ltd. Domicile: 6/F, Hongye Building, No. 25 Tianshan Road, Shantou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Gui Zhenliang, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Shen Xiaowei, Attorney at Law, Beijing Dingming Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited. Domicile: 14/F, Bank of China Tower, No. 1 Garden Road, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Representative: He Guangbei, President of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shouzhi, Attorney at Law, Beijing King & Wood Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Qian Yaozi, Attorney at Law, Beijing King & Wood Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shantou Special Economic Zone Xinye Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: 20/F, Jinlong Building, Hengshan Road, Shantou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Lin Zhaoxu, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

The appellant, Shantou Hongye (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongye Company), appealed to this Court regarding a dispute over a guarantee contract with the appellees, Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited (hereinafter referred to as BOC Hong Kong) and Shantou Special Economic Zone Xinye Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinye Company), against the civil judgment (2000) Yue Fa Jing Er Chu Zi No. 5 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wang Yun and Acting Judges Ren Xuefeng and Chen Jizhong to hold a public hearing in this case. Xinye Company failed to appear in court to defend without justifiable reasons. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On November 28, 1997, Xinye Company sent an "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" to Chiyu Banking Corporation Limited: "Whereas you have made or agreed to make loans, grant overdrafts or other banking facilities to Dalifeng Group Limited (hereinafter referred to as the Borrower), the undersigned company/entity (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantor) hereby issues an unconditional and irrevocable guarantee deed in your favor. The guarantee obligations are as follows: 1. The Guarantor guarantees that the Borrower shall, in accordance with the provisions of the relevant loan agreement or other agreement, including any amendments concerning the content thereof (hereinafter referred to as the Agreement), repay the principal, interest, charges, and other amounts payable (hereinafter referred to as the Indebtedness) on time. 2. If the Borrower violates any provision of the Agreement or delays in repaying the Indebtedness, the Guarantor shall, within seven days of receiving the relevant written notice from you, immediately repay all Indebtedness of the Borrower in the currency specified in the Agreement and remit the amount by telegraphic transfer to the account designated by you. The Guarantor accepts that the written proof provided by you showing the amount owed to you by the Borrower under the Agreement is accurate and shall not raise any objection. 3. This guarantee deed shall guarantee the Borrower's repayment to you of any loans, overdrafts, or other banking facilities granted at any time and the final balances thereof in accordance with the Agreement, and shall continue in full force and effect until all Indebtedness of the Borrower to you is fully repaid. Provided, however, that the liability of the Guarantor under this guarantee deed shall not exceed HKD 313,000,000.00, plus interest thereon and legal costs and other expenses incurred by you in recovering the Indebtedness. 4. The Guarantor undertakes that all amounts payable under this guarantee deed shall be paid in full without any set-off, deduction, or withholding of taxes or any amounts of any nature. If, by reason of any legal provisions or other circumstances, the Guarantor is compelled to withhold or deduct any taxes or other amounts from the amounts payable, the Guarantor undertakes to pay an additional amount to ensure that the net amount actually received by you equals the full amount which would have been receivable had no such withholding or deduction been made. 5. You may deposit any amounts received under this guarantee deed into any account or temporarily credit them to an account. 6. Regardless of whether the Agreement or any part thereof is valid or enforceable, this guarantee deed shall continue in full force and effect, be irrevocable, and be unconditional until the Borrower fully repays all Indebtedness. 7. This guarantee deed constitutes the Guarantor's direct liability to you and shall not be affected or rendered void by: (i) any personnel changes, restructuring, merger, reorganization, name change, bankruptcy, or liquidation of the Borrower, the Guarantor, or you; (ii) the Borrower exceeding its borrowing authority; (iii) any dispute, controversy, or contract between the Borrower and the Guarantor or other guarantors; (iv) any debt restructuring between the Borrower or the Guarantor and the creditor; (v) the invalidity or unenforceability of the Borrower's obligations under the Agreement for any reason; or (vi) any amendment to the content of the Agreement and/or the loans, overdrafts, or other banking facilities. You may treat the Guarantor as the principal debtor and pursue the Indebtedness from the Guarantor. 8. The liability under this guarantee deed shall not be affected by any indulgence or extension of time for repayment of the Indebtedness granted by you to the Borrower, or any other indulgence, arrangement, or compromise, or by your delay in exercising any rights under the Agreement. 9. This guarantee deed is independent of any collateral or security now or hereafter held by you from the Borrower or any other person as security for the Indebtedness, and its validity shall not be affected by, nor shall it affect, any other guarantee deed or collateral or security. 10. You shall not be required first to take any action against the Borrower or any other guarantor or any collateral or security before proceeding against the Guarantor under this guarantee deed. 11. Until all Indebtedness is fully repaid or with your prior written consent, the Guarantor agrees not to exercise any right of subrogation, set-off, or counterclaim obtained from the Borrower, nor any right exercisable over the Borrower's assets. 12. With respect to the Guarantor's obligations to you under this guarantee deed, you may exercise rights of set-off and lien over any deposits of the Guarantor in any account with you and any securities, stocks, or other pledged items held by you, without prior notice. 13. The Guarantor acknowledges that the execution and performance of this guarantee deed constitute a commercial act, and the Guarantor does not have any immunity from jurisdiction, legal process, set-off, or execution of property or other legal claims on the ground that the Guarantor is a member or department of the state or government. The Guarantor shall not, on sovereign or any other grounds, request or claim any immunity from any legal action or proceedings, or from the attachment of the Guarantor's assets in any jurisdiction or the enforcement of any judgment in respect of the Guarantor's obligations under this guarantee deed, and the Guarantor hereby irrevocably waives such immunity. 14. All notices from you to the Guarantor, if sent by post to the address below or to any other address notified by the Guarantor to you, shall be deemed to have been received by the Guarantor five days after posting, regardless of whether the notice is subsequently returned to you. If sent by telex, the notice shall be deemed to have been received by the Guarantor at the time of dispatch. 15. The Guarantor hereby warrants and declares that it has the legal capacity to execute this guarantee deed and perform its obligations, and has obtained all necessary authorizations and completed all formalities and obtained all requisite approvals and consents from any government or other department/entity for providing this guarantee deed. 16. The Guarantor hereby undertakes that the Guarantor shall at all times take all necessary actions or execute all necessary documents to ensure the legal validity and binding effect of this guarantee deed. 17. If this guarantee deed is executed by more than one guarantor, the liability of the guarantors shall be joint and several. You may release or refrain from pursuing any one guarantor without affecting any of your rights under this guarantee deed against the other guarantors. 18. The legal representatives, successors, agents, and receivers of the Guarantor shall be bound by the terms of this guarantee deed and shall perform the obligations hereunder. 19. After the Indebtedness of the Borrower is repaid, you shall be entitled to retain this guarantee deed for six months before canceling or returning it to the Guarantor. During such period, if the Borrower becomes bankrupt or is liquidated, you may continue to retain this guarantee deed and any related collaterals until further notice from you. 20. The laws of Hong Kong shall govern this guarantee deed, and the courts of Hong Kong shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes arising under this guarantee deed." The letter bears the signature of witness Lin Jingqian (staff of Bank of China, Shantou), the seal of Xinye Company, and the name of Lin Zhaoxu, then Deputy General Manager of Xinye Company.

The letter bears the signature of witness Lin Jingqian, the seal of Hongye Company, and the private seal of its then legal representative, Cai Chengtong.

On September 2, 1998, Chiyu Banking Corporation Limited issued a "General Facility Letter" file number P/113/98HKL to the Dalifeng Group, the content of which is as follows:

1. Distribution of Facilities

1.1 The facilities shall be provided by the following methods: (1) Overdraft facility not exceeding HKD 2,000,000. The annual overdraft interest rate shall be the higher of the HKD Prime Rate (Prime Rate) as determined by us from time to time or the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (overnight) plus 1% (whether before or after judgment). The current annual interest rate for this overdraft facility is 11%, but this rate may fluctuate from time to time; (2) Overdraft facility not exceeding HKD 26,000,000. The annual overdraft interest rate shall be the higher of the HKD Prime Rate (Prime Rate) as determined by us from time to time or the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (overnight) plus 2% (whether before or after judgment). The current annual interest rate for this overdraft facility is 12%, but this rate may fluctuate from time to time; (3) Letter of credit issuance and import bill advance facility not exceeding HKD 160,000,000 (including trust receipts for a period of 120 days, and trust receipts not exceeding HKD 135,000,000 secured by export letters of credit deposited with us and valued at not less than HKD 72,000,000); (4) Negotiation guarantee facility under export letters of credit not exceeding HKD 120,000,000; (5) Packing loan facility not exceeding HKD 40,000,000 and/or 70% of the value of export letters of credit deposited with us, whichever is the lesser, and not exceeding 90 days or the expiry date of the letter of credit, whichever is earlier; (6) Back-to-back letter of credit issuance and import bill advance facility not exceeding HKD 40,000,000, applicable only to "direct shipment" situations; (7) Mortgage loan of HKD 30,950,000, subject to the conditions set out in our letter dated January 7, 1997, file number 0039/C/97HKL; (8) Mortgage loan of HKD 3,570,000, subject to the conditions set out in our letter dated October 11, 1996, file number 2114/C/96HKL.

1.2 We reserve the absolute discretion to accept or reject any application by you for the use of any of the above facilities.

1.3 When we make payment or incur liability in respect of the relevant facility, the above facility shall be automatically deemed to have been drawn down by you and/or lent by us.

1.4 Without prejudice to clause 3 below, we reserve the right to reallocate the various banking facilities at our sole and absolute discretion at any time.

2. Interest rates and calculation methods

2.1 With respect to all amounts lent/drawn down under the facilities, we shall charge interest, commission, and/or other fees specified in this letter, or at the standard rates specified in any rate schedule published by us from time to time (whether before or after judgment).

2.2 Interest shall be calculated on the basis of actual days. For HKD loans, interest shall be calculated on the basis of 365 days per year; for USD loans, on the basis of 360 days per year; and for other currencies, in accordance with market practice.

2.3 All accrued interest shall be paid on the dates designated by us in accordance with market practice. If not paid as required, such interest shall be capitalized and shall itself bear interest.

2.4 We are entitled to charge excess/late payment interest on any amount exceeding the agreed limit or overdue. Unless otherwise agreed between us and you from time to time or at any time, such amounts shall bear interest at an annual rate equal to the higher of the prime cost of funds as determined by us from time to time plus 10% (whether before or after judgment), calculated from the date of default until the actual full repayment of the amount overdue, provided that we may change the basis for calculating late payment interest by giving prior notice to you.

3. Expiry of facilities. We shall conduct periodic reviews of your facilities. When we issue a notice of termination of facilities to you, all facilities shall terminate immediately. The facilities currently provided to you shall continue until the issuance of such notice of termination. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this letter, we reserve the sole and absolute discretion to increase, decrease, or cancel the facilities or any part thereof at any time, and such change shall take effect immediately upon our notification to you on the same day.

4. Repayment

4.1 We have the overriding right to demand that you immediately repay all facilities and accrued interest.

4.2 All payments made by you to the Bank shall be based on the original currency of the amounts or obligations paid or incurred by the Bank under the facility, and shall be made in immediately available funds, free and clear of any set-off or counterclaim, and without any deduction or withholding for or on account of any and all present or future taxes, duties, or other charges.

4.3 If any payment is not made in the correct currency, the Bank may, at its sole discretion, convert such payment into the correct currency at the Bank's spot rate of exchange conclusively determined by the Bank, in order to discharge your debts and obligations denominated in that currency.

4.4 At the time of payment by you or at any time thereafter, the Bank shall have the exclusive and absolute right to appropriate any payment made by you to the Bank or any moneys held or controlled by the Bank towards the discharge of any part of your indebtedness to the Bank (such part to be determined by the Bank as it sees fit). Any such appropriation shall override any appropriation purported to be made by you.

5. Processing Fee: You shall pay a processing fee of HKD 5,000 upon acceptance of this letter (which fee shall in no event be refundable) and thereafter an annual fee of HKD 3,000 or such other amount as agreed between the Bank and you upon each renewal of the facility.

6. Security and Documents: The Bank will provide the facility to you upon receipt of the following documents, together with such other documents as the Bank may from time to time require, and upon determining that the form and content of such documents are satisfactory:
(1) A guarantee deed duly executed by Chen Shaoying, Fang Runping, and Lin Zhaoxu, relating to the repayment of not less than HKD 396.52 million in principal, together with accrued interest and overdue interest thereon, and other fees and expenses as set forth in such guarantee deed;
(2) A guarantee deed duly executed by Hongye Company and Xinye Company, relating to the repayment of not less than HKD 313 million in principal, together with accrued interest and overdue interest thereon, and other fees and expenses as set forth in such guarantee deed, together with relevant board resolutions;
(3) A set-off and deposit mortgage deed, indemnity, deposit mortgage and set-off deed, and deposit transfer deed, duly executed in favor of the Bank, constituting a first fixed charge over deposits of not less than HKD 49 million, together with relevant board resolutions (if applicable);
(4) Legal charges/equitable mortgages over the following properties, the titles of which have been verified by solicitors appointed by the Bank:
A. Unit 3, 18th Floor, Office Tower, Convention and Exhibition Centre, 1 Harbour Road, Hong Kong;
B. Flat D, 6th Floor, Block 3, Phase 12, Whampoa Garden, Kowloon.
I. The properties shall be insured against fire with an insurance company acceptable to the Bank, with the insured amount being the facility amount or such other amount as the Bank deems appropriate;
II. The relevant insurance policies shall be assigned to the Bank and delivered to the Bank together with premium receipts; and
III. The Bank shall be entitled (but not obliged) to purchase the above insurance on your behalf, and all insurance premiums, valuation fees (if any), and expenses shall be borne by you, and the Bank shall be entitled to debit such amounts from your account without reference to you.

7. Conclusive Accounts: Any statement of account relating to the facility, if signed by any officer of the Bank certifying it to be correct, shall be conclusive evidence of your indebtedness to the Bank and binding on you (except for manifest error).

8. Further Covenants: All corporate resolutions necessary for the execution and performance of this letter have been duly passed by your shareholders, directors, and authorized officers in accordance with the laws of Hong Kong, the laws of your place of incorporation, and your memorandum and articles of association. This letter constitutes legal, valid, and binding obligations on you.

9. Waiver and Accumulation of Rights: No delay or failure on the part of the Bank in exercising any right, power, privilege, or remedy under this letter shall impair or be deemed to be a waiver thereof. A single or partial exercise of any such right, power, privilege, or remedy shall not preclude any further exercise thereof. The rights, powers, privileges, and remedies provided in this letter are cumulative and are not exclusive of any rights, powers, privileges, or remedies provided by law.

10. Authorization for Debit: The Bank shall be entitled at any time and from time to time (without notice to you) to debit from any of your accounts all or any interest, fees, charges, commissions, outgoings, expenses, and other sums due and payable by you under this facility. Such sums shall be deemed to have been duly withdrawn or overdrawn from your account.

11. Costs: All costs shall be borne by you on a full indemnity basis.

12. Governing Law: The laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The minutes of the board meeting of Xinye Company, signed by Chen Jianshen (as Chairman of the meeting), Liu Quanhui (as Director), and also bearing the signatures of Xinye Company directors Chen Jianshen, Liu Quanhui, Chen Shaona, Chen Jianhong, Chen Shubo, Qiu Xuewan, and Chen Yuhua, and affixed with the company seal of Xinye Company, recorded as follows: The board of directors of Xinye Company convened a meeting on November 28, 1997, at 20/F, Jinlong Building, Hengshan Road, Shantou City. All directors of the company received notice of the meeting, and the dispatch of the meeting notice complied with the provisions of the company's articles of association; the convening of the meeting met the notice requirements. In accordance with the company's articles of association, all directors attended the meeting. The meeting was presided over by the chairman. The following is the record of the meeting: (1) The meeting was informed that the Dalifeng Group (the borrower) had utilized a bank facility of not less than HKD 395.83 million from Guohua Bank (the lender) (the Facility); (2) At the request of the borrower, as one of the conditions for guaranteeing the borrower's repayment of the Facility, the company was required to execute an "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" to guarantee to the lender all amounts owed by the borrower to the lender from time to time, with the company's maximum liability under the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" being HKD 313 million plus interest and related expenses; (3) The company's articles of association permit the company to enter into the above transaction; (4) If any director/shareholder had a direct or indirect interest in the above transaction, such director/shareholder had made a declaration to the board and disclosed the details and nature of such interest. All directors/shareholders of the company had a direct or indirect interest in the transaction, and the board had been fully informed and confirmed; (5) The board carefully studied the above matters and related documents. After thorough discussion, all attending directors unanimously resolved to pass the following resolutions:

1. The company agreed to provide a guarantee to Guohua Bank in the amount of HKD 313 million plus interest and related expenses, guaranteeing the performance by the Dalifeng Group of any loan agreement with Guohua Bank;
2. The company had reviewed, agreed to, and accepted the full contents of the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed";
3. The company authorized Lin Zhaoxu to fully represent the company in executing and affixing the company seal to the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" and to take all actions related thereto on behalf of the company;
4. The company fully understood that the lender would only provide or continue to provide the above facility to the borrower on the condition that the company issued the guarantee, and also understood that the issuance of the guarantee by the company must comply with the laws and regulations of the PRC, and the company would be responsible for handling the relevant procedures and bearing all liability.

Chairman's signature: Chen Jianshen; Directors' signatures: Liu Quanhui, Chen Shaona, Chen Jianhong, Chen Shubo, Qiu Xuewan, Chen Yuhua.

The board of directors of Hongye Company convened a meeting on April 17, 1998, at the Hongye Building, Tianshan Road, Shantou City, Guangdong Province. The minutes of the meeting recorded: All directors of the company received notice of the meeting, and the dispatch of the meeting notice complied with the provisions of the company's articles of association; the convening of the meeting met the notice requirements. In accordance with the company's articles of association, all directors attended the meeting. The following is the record of the meeting: (1) The meeting was informed that the Dalifeng Group (hereinafter referred to as the borrower) had utilized a bank facility of HKD 395.87 million from Guohua Bank (the lender) (the Facility); (2) At the request of the borrower, as one of the conditions for guaranteeing the borrower's repayment of the Facility, the company was required to provide a guarantee to the lender in the amount of HKD 313 million plus interest and related expenses; (3) The company's articles of association permit the company to enter into the above transaction; (4) If any director/shareholder had a direct or indirect interest in the above transaction, such director/shareholder had made a declaration to the board and disclosed the details and nature of such interest. All directors/shareholders of the company had a direct or indirect interest in the transaction, and the board had been fully informed and confirmed; (5) The board carefully studied the above matters and related documents. After thorough discussion, all attending directors unanimously resolved to pass the following resolutions:

1. The company agreed to provide a guarantee to Guohua Bank in the amount of HKD 313 million plus related expenses, guaranteeing the performance by the Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. of any loan agreement with Guohua Bank;
2. The company had reviewed, agreed to, and accepted the full contents of the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed";
3. The company authorized Cai Chengtong to fully represent the company in executing and affixing the company seal to the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed";
4. The company fully understood that the lender would only provide or continue to provide the above facility to the borrower on the condition that the company issued the guarantee, and also understood that the issuance of the guarantee by the company must comply with the laws and regulations of the PRC regarding the handling of approval, registration, or filing procedures (including but not limited to listing and foreign exchange management), and the company would be responsible for handling such procedures. If the guarantee contract becomes invalid due to the failure to handle the procedures required by PRC law, the company shall bear full responsibility and compensate the lender for all losses suffered as a result of the lender's continued provision of the above facility now or in the future.

On January 3, 2000, the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, in Winding-Up Case No. 883 of 1999, confirmed that Guohua Bank's claims against Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. totaled HKD 4,408,215,707 and USD 25,771,093.15, plus interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61. On May 22 of the same year, the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd., Ernst & Young Hong Kong, by way of a letter from lawyer Liao Yaoqiang (File No. NC/PY/DC/st/0005-LI0953), confirmed that Guohua Bank's claims against Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. comprised principal of HKD 4,408,215,707 and USD 25,771,093.15, and interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61; Hongye Company and Xinye Company were the domestic guarantors for the above loans, and each guarantor's liability under its respective guarantee deed did not exceed HKD 313 million.

Separately, on November 17, 1999, Gu Kairen Law Firm, Hong Kong, sent letters to Hongye Company and Xinye Company respectively titled "Re: Debt Owed by Dalifeng Group (Borrower) to Guohua Bank," stating: Our firm is instructed by Guohua Bank to address this letter to your company concerning the repayment of the borrower's debt. Pursuant to an Irrevocable Guarantee Deed (the Guarantee) dated November 28, 1997, your company, as guarantor, has guaranteed to our client the repayment of the borrower's debts owed to our client. Based on information provided by our client, the borrower has failed to repay its debts to our client on schedule. As of November 11, 1999, the total debt owed by the borrower to our client amounted to HKD 37,353,037.48 and USD 26,122,045.32. For details of the relevant debts, please refer to the schedule attached to this letter. Our firm now, as instructed by our client, hereby demands that your company immediately repay the entire debt of the above borrower, together with related interest and our firm's legal fees in connection with the issuance of this letter (HKD 2,000). Should our firm undertake further work on the above matter at our client's request, our legal fees will increase accordingly. Please confirm the amount of interest with our client when arranging payment of the relevant debt. If, within seven days from the date of this letter, our client or our firm has not received payment of the above debt from your company, our firm will, as instructed by our client and without further notice to your company, take appropriate legal action to recover the above debt, all accumulated interest, and all expenses incurred thereby.

On November 29, 1999, Shantou Foreign Economic Law Firm replied to Gu Kairen Law Firm, Hong Kong: This lawyer, instructed by Hongye Company, responds to the matters stated in your firm's lawyer's letter dated November 17, 1999, as follows: 1. The "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" is a void declaration and has no legal binding effect on Hongye Company. This is because, according to Article 24 of the "Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Foreign Exchange," "foreign guarantees may only be provided by financial institutions and enterprises that meet the conditions prescribed by the state and must be approved by the foreign exchange administration authority." The "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" was not so approved. 2. This lawyer suggests that the Dalifeng Group and Guohua Bank resolve their dispute through negotiation.

On November 10, 2000, Wen Wuyong, lawyer of Guangdong Zhongda Law Firm, sent a letter to Guohua Bank: Re: The matter of Hongye Company not having provided a guarantee for the borrowing of the Dalifeng Group from Guohua Bank. This lawyer, instructed by Hongye Company, writes to your bank regarding the aforementioned loan guarantee. Upon review of the minutes of shareholders' general meetings and board meetings of Hongye Company, no shareholders' general meeting or board meeting was held on April 17, 1998, and no resolution was passed to provide a guarantee for the borrowing of HKD 313 million by Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank. According to Article 94 of the Articles of Association of Hongye Company: "The board of directors shall exercise the following powers: ... (8) Decide on the company's asset mortgages and other guarantee matters within the range of 20% of the company's net assets at the time." That is, the board of directors of Hongye Company has the authority to approve guarantees only up to 20% of the company's net assets. In April 1998, the net assets of Hongye Company were RMB 252,204,200. The board of directors of Hongye Company had no authority to decide on a guarantee exceeding the company's net assets; a guarantee exceeding the company's net assets should be decided by the shareholders' general meeting. According to investigations, Cai Chengtong, the chairman and legal representative of Hongye Company, confirmed that no shareholders' general meeting or board meeting was ever convened to discuss or decide on providing a guarantee for the borrowing of Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank. Guohua Bank never sent any representative to meet with Chairman Cai Chengtong of Hongye Company to discuss the guarantee matter. Hongye Company never issued any "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" or "Board Resolution of Shantou Hongye (Group) Co., Ltd." to Guohua Bank. Furthermore, upon inspection of the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" and "Board Resolution" of Hongye Company submitted by your bank to the court via the Guangdong High People's Court, Chairman Cai Chengtong and the directors of Hongye Company stated that they had never seen the above guarantee deed or board resolution. Moreover, the above "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" and "Board Resolution" bear no signatures of the chairman or directors of Hongye Company. Therefore, the above guarantee deed and board resolution are legally invalid. In summary, this lawyer believes that your bank's lawsuit against Hongye Company based on the above invalid "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" and "Board Resolution" is unfounded in law. At the same time, your bank's litigation will cause reputational damage to Hongye Company, a listed company, and Hongye Company will use legal weapons to protect its own rights and interests.

From December 4 to 6, 2000, the then directors of Hongye Company, Cai Chengtong, Zheng Zhixiong, Xu Junzhao, Zhou Yingqi, Rui Yiping, and Huang Chuwen, each issued notarized "Declarations," the main content of which was substantially similar: I have been a director of Hongye Company from May 1996 to the present. On April 17, 1998, I did not convene any shareholders' general meeting or board meeting to discuss or decide on providing a guarantee for the borrowing of HKD 313 million and related expenses by Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank. I have never signed any "Board Resolution" or "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" providing a guarantee for the borrowing of HKD 313 million and related expenses by Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank. Guohua Bank has never sent any representative to discuss with me the matter of providing a guarantee for the borrowing of Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank; Hongye Company never issued any "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" or "Board Resolution" to Guohua Bank to provide a guarantee for the borrowing of Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. from Guohua Bank. In addition, according to Article 94 of the Articles of Association of Hongye Company, the board of directors has no authority to decide on providing a guarantee for a borrowing of HKD 313 million. So declared. Attached to each declaration was a list of directors of Hongye Company as of April 1998, provided by Hongye Company on February 12, 2001, which included 11 directors: Cai Chengtong, Huang Chuwen, Wang Banglin, Rui Yiping, Zhou Yingqi, Li Zhuangke, Xu Junzhao, Zheng Hanqin, Chen Yifeng, Cao Dai, and Zheng Zhixiong.

During the litigation, Hongye Company submitted to the court two pieces of evidence: (1) an "Irrevocable Loan Guarantee" dated October 17, 1997, for a loan of RMB 2 million from Shantou Hongye King Kong Industrial Company to Shantou Urban Cooperative Bank; and (2) a joint and several guarantee for a "Loan Contract" dated May 27, 1998, for a loan of RMB 1.38 million from Shantou Hongye King Kong Industrial Company to Shantou Urban Cooperative Bank. The seal affixed by Hongye Company on these two pieces of evidence was consistent with the seal affixed on the "Irrevocable Guarantee Deed" issued by Hongye Company to Guohua Bank in this case.

On March 20, 2001, the court of first instance inquired with the Shantou Public Security Bureau regarding the impression of the seal used by Hongye Company in 1998, but the bureau orally replied that the records had been destroyed.

As a dispute arose between Guohua Bank and Hongye Company and Xinye Company over the repayment of the amounts, and negotiations failed to resolve the matter, Guohua Bank filed a lawsuit against Hongye Company and Xinye Company as defendants in the court of first instance, requesting that the two defendants at first instance be jointly and severally liable for the loan of HKD 44,082,157.07 and USD 25,771,093.15, plus interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61, owed by Dalifeng Group Co., Ltd. under the facility, and bear all litigation costs in this case.

The court of first instance found that: Xinye Company and Hongye Company provided guarantees to Guohua Bank for the above-mentioned sums on November 28, 1997 and April 17, 1998, respectively. Xinye Company did not submit a defense or make a plea. The guarantee represented its true intention and was established in accordance with law. Hongye Company argued that the official seal affixed to the guarantee instrument was not its company seal and that the Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution and the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed of Hongye Company provided by Guohua Bank were forgeries. However, Hongye Company failed to provide the imprint of its company seal reviewed by the public security department in 1998. Moreover, among the evidence submitted by Hongye Company to this court, there were the official seal used by Hongye Company at that time and the private seal of its legal representative Cai Chengtong, which were consistent with the seals on the guarantee instrument in this case. Furthermore, the General Credit Facility Letter (Bank File No. P/113/98HKL) dated September 2, 1998 from Guohua Bank stipulated: "When the Bank receives the following documents and other documents as the Bank may from time to time require, and determines that the form and content of such documents are satisfactory, the Bank will provide you with credit facilities: ... a guarantee deed duly executed by Hongye Company and Xinye Company, which deed relates to the repayment of a principal amount of not less than HKD 313 million together with accrued interest and overdue interest thereon and other costs and expenses as stated in the said guarantee deed, together with the relevant board resolution. ..." The guaranteed creditor's rights were confirmed by the High Court of Hong Kong in Companies Winding-up Case No. 883 of 1999, totaling HKD 44,082,157.07, USD 25,771,093.15, and interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61. That is to say, Dalifeng Group Limited had obtained the credit facility from Guohua Bank, thus confirming that Guohua Bank had received the guarantee instruments from Hongye Company and Xinye Company. As for the post-hoc testimonies of the directors of Hongye Company's board, the directors failed to appear for cross-examination in court, and the testimonies were unilateral evidence, which should not be accepted as admissible evidence. Therefore, this court found that Hongye Company's guarantee was established.

This case involves a guarantee dispute. The guarantee instruments issued by Hongye Company and Xinye Company stated that Hong Kong law applied. Since the creditors guaranteed by Hongye Company and Xinye Company were enterprises registered in Hong Kong, this case concerns an external guarantee. Hongye Company and Xinye Company did not actually complete the approval procedures with the foreign exchange control authorities. China is a country with foreign exchange controls, and Chinese laws mandatorily require that external guarantees be approved by the foreign exchange control authorities. Pursuant to Article 150 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the application of foreign laws or international practices in accordance with the provisions of this chapter shall not violate the social public interests of the People's Republic of China," and Article 194 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "acts of parties evading mandatory or prohibitive legal norms of China shall not have the effect of applying foreign laws," the agreement of Hongye Company and Xinye Company in the guarantee instrument to apply Hong Kong law constituted an act of evading the mandatory or prohibitive legal norms of China. This agreement is not legally binding within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the validity of the guarantee instrument should be determined in accordance with the laws of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 7 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "civil activities shall respect social morality and shall not harm the social public interests, undermine the national economic plan, or disrupt the social economic order," and Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "an external guarantee contract shall be invalid under any of the following circumstances: (1) the external guarantee has not been approved or registered by the relevant competent state authority; ..." The guarantees provided by Hongye Company and Xinye Company to Guohua Bank were not approved or registered by the relevant competent state authority, thereby violating the principle of public order and good customs of China and lacking legal effect. Hongye Company and Xinye Company both promised in their deeds of guarantee and board resolutions to ensure that the guarantees were approved by the government, and that they would bear all liability if the guarantees were invalid due to failure to complete the procedures required by law. Therefore, the liability for the invalidity of the guarantees in this case should be borne entirely by Hongye Company and Xinye Company. The legal consequences arising therefrom should be determined in accordance with Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "if the main contract is valid and the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the economic losses of the creditor under the main contract; ..." Accordingly, Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the debts in this case.

In summary, Guohua Bank's claim that Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the debts in this case is legally well-founded and is supported; Guohua Bank's assertion that the guarantees provided by Hongye Company and Xinye Company are valid is contrary to the laws of the People's Republic of China and is not adopted. Pursuant to Article 150 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 138, 147, and 149 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, jointly and severally compensate Guohua Bank for the principal amount of HKD 44,082,157.07 and USD 25,771,093.15, interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61 (calculated up to January 3, 2000), and interest on the said principal amounts from January 4, 2000 until the date of full payment (calculated at the interest rate stipulated in Guohua Bank's General Credit Facility Letter, Bank File No. P/113/98HKL, dated September 2, 1998).

The case acceptance fees of USD 142,408.05 and HKD 227,456.98, and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 322,828, shall be borne jointly by Hongye Company and Xinye Company. Guohua Bank has prepaid the case acceptance fees of USD 142,408.05 and HKD 227,456.98, and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 322,828. Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall pay the amounts due directly to Guohua Bank, and this court will not refund them.

Hongye Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this court arguing: First, the court of first instance erred in finding that the guarantee contract in this case represented the true intention of Hongye Company. 1. After the first instance trial, relevant criminal judicial materials showed that the guarantee contract in this case was forged through collusion between Fang Zeping, the former acting general manager of Hongye Company, and Chen Shaoying, the general manager of Hong Kong Dalifeng Company, and their actions were suspected of constituting a loan fraud crime. Therefore, the guarantee contract is invalid due to illegality. Pursuant to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Criminal Suspects, Hongye Company requests that this case be transferred to the public security authority for priority handling. 2. The issuance of the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed by Hongye Company to Guohua Bank did not represent the true intention of Hongye Company and constituted an ultra vires act. The board of directors is the organ that expresses the intention of a company. The board of directors of Hongye Company never passed a board resolution on the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed on April 17, 1998. The Hongye Company Board Resolution in this case is purely fictitious. Therefore, although the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed made pursuant to the Board Resolution bears the official seal of Hongye Company, it does not constitute the true intention of Hongye Company. On the contrary, any personnel of Hongye Company affixing the official seal constituted an ultra vires act. 3. Guohua Bank failed to exercise due diligence in reviewing the guarantee documents in this case and was clearly at fault in the process of accepting the guarantee. It should be presumed that Guohua Bank should have known of the ultra vires guarantee in this case, and the guarantee contract should have no legal effect on it. Second, the court of first instance erred in directly recognizing the creditor's rights declared by Guohua Bank to the Hong Kong Official Receiver's Office as the main creditor's rights in this case. Hongye Company enjoys the right to raise defenses of the principal debtor, including but not limited to defenses against the authenticity of the amount of the creditor's rights. Third, the court of first instance improperly applied the law. The court of first instance found that the guarantee contract in this case represented the true intention, but that the external guarantee was invalid for lack of approval by the relevant competent state authority, and that Hongye Company was entirely at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee. This finding clearly involved improper application of the law. Guohua Bank bears an inescapable fault for the invalidity of the guarantee. Additionally, during the hearing in this court, Hongye Company raised objections to the facts found in the original judgment regarding the letter dated November 17, 1997 from Hong Kong Gu Kairen Law Firm to Hongye Company concerning "Matters Regarding the Outstanding Debt of Dalifeng Group Limited (Borrower) to Guohua Bank" and the reply letter dated November 29, 1999 from Shantou Foreign Economic Law Firm on behalf of Hongye Company to Hong Kong Gu Kairen Law Firm. In summary, Hongye Company requests: 1. This case involves suspected economic crimes. Hongye Company requests that after ascertaining the facts, the appellate court quash the original judgment and transfer the case to the public security authority for priority handling. 2. The first instance procedure was seriously illegal. Hongye Company requests that the appellate court quash the original judgment and remand the case for retrial. 3. The original judgment found unclear facts and improperly applied the law. Hongye Company requests that the appellate court amend the judgment or remand the case for retrial in accordance with law. 4. The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by the appellee.

BOC Hong Kong argued in its defense: First, the finding in the original judgment that the guarantee contract in this case represented the true intention of Hongye Company is entirely correct. 1. The evidence listed by Hongye Company cannot prove its claim that the Hongye Company Board Resolution and the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed were fictitious. This case is an economic dispute. Although some natural persons were involved in economic crimes in other cases, it is unrelated to this case and can be fully tried separately from this case. This situation falls within the scope of Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Criminal Suspects, and Hongye Company's claim should not be supported. 2. The Irrevocable Guarantee Deed issued by Hongye Company is lawful and valid. Hongye Company's claim of "untrue intention and ultra vires act" cannot be established. The board resolution is an internal document of Hongye Company. What has external legal effect on the company is the Irrevocable Guarantee Deed, not the board resolution. 3. The appellee accepted the guarantee instrument in reliance on Hongye Company's promises and assurances. It is untenable for Hongye Company to deny the validity of the guarantee deed by invoking its internal management procedures. Second, the creditor's rights determined by the Hong Kong Official Receiver's Office should be recognized as the main creditor's rights in this case. Third, the application of law in the original judgment was correct. Hongye Company failed to fulfill the obligation to apply for approval for the external guarantee in accordance with the Guarantee Law of China, resulting in the invalidity of the guarantee contract for violating the mandatory provisions of national law. Hongye Company is entirely at fault for this invalidity and shall bear full liability for compensation. Therefore, Hongye Company's appeal should be dismissed.

Xinye Company neither filed an appeal nor submitted a defense.

This court, upon trial, finds the following: At the first instance of this case, Guohua Bank provided the court of first instance with the Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution of Hongye Company dated April 17, 1998, which bore the seal of Hongye Company. Hongye Company raised an objection to the authenticity of the said Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution, which was not sustained by the court of first instance. On appeal, Hongye Company still objected to this part of the facts, arguing that the said Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution was false. However, it now does not deny the authenticity of the company seal affixed to the Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution. Hongye Company stated that its board resolutions were all numbered in chronological order and provided three consecutively numbered Board of Directors' Meeting Resolutions of the company, namely Shan Hong Dong Jue Zi [1998] No. 019, 020, and 021, which were adopted on April 6, 1998, April 21, 1998, and August 5, 1998, respectively, to prove that the board meeting of the company was not held on April 17, 1998. Hongye Company also provided notarized Declarations separately issued by the then directors of the company, Cai Chengtong, Zheng Zhixiong, Xu Junzhao, Zhou Yingqi, Rui Yiping, and Huang Chuwen, all of whom denied in the Declarations that a board meeting was held on April 17, 1998 and that the said Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution was issued. Moreover, according to Article 111 of the company's articles of association provided by Hongye Company, directors should sign the board resolution, but the Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution involved in this case bore no signature of any director. This court finds that, although the seal of Hongye Company on the said Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution is genuine, based on a comprehensive analysis of the evidentiary materials provided by the parties, this court determines that Hongye Company did not hold a board meeting on April 17, 1998 to discuss the guarantee matters, and the authenticity of the content recorded in the said Hongye Company Board of Directors' Meeting Resolution is not confirmed. During the hearing in this court, Hongye Company also objected to the facts found in the original judgment regarding the letter dated November 17, 1997 from Hong Kong Gu Kairen Law Firm to Hongye Company concerning "Matters Regarding the Outstanding Debt of Dalifeng Group Limited (Borrower) to Guohua Bank" and the reply letter dated November 29, 1999 from Shantou Foreign Economic Law Firm on behalf of Hongye Company to Hong Kong Gu Kairen Law Firm. The court of first instance made its finding on this part of the facts based on the corresponding letters provided by Guohua Bank. Although Hongye Company objected to this, it merely stated its claim without providing any evidence to deny the authenticity of the above letters. Therefore, this court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance regarding this part, and Hongye Company's objection to this part of the facts is not sustained.

As for the other facts found by the court of first instance, all are supported by corresponding evidence, and the appellant Hongye Company did not raise any objection. This court also confirms them.

This court further finds: Pursuant to the Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited (Merger) Ordinance passed in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in July 2001, the entire assets and liabilities of 10 Hong Kong banks, including Guohua Commercial Bank, Hong Kong Branch, were injected into Po Sang Bank Limited. Po Sang Bank Limited officially changed its name to Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited on October 1, 2001. From October 1, 2001, the entire assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations of Guohua Commercial Bank, Hong Kong Branch, are enjoyed and borne by Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited.

On November 24, 2003, the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Limited, Yiu Leung Keung, by letter file reference SLIU/GH/st/0311-L31854, again confirmed that the amount of Guohua Bank's creditor's rights against Dalifeng Company was principal amounts of HKD 44,082,157.07 and USD 25,771,093.15, and interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61; Hongye Company and Xinye Company were both domestic guarantors of the above loans, and the liability of each guarantor under its respective guarantee deed did not exceed HKD 313 million.

Furthermore, during the proceedings in this court, Hongye Company provided this court with evidentiary materials including the report form for investigating a major criminal case in Shantou City, Guangdong Province, the "Letter of Transfer Regarding the Suspected Loan Fraud Case of Fang Zeping (also known as Fang Yanping) and Chen Shaoying" from the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of Shantou Municipal Public Security Bureau to the Xicheng Sub-bureau of the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau, the Indictment (Jing Jian Yi Fen Xing Su Zi [2001] No. 314) of the First Branch of the Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate, and the Criminal Judgment (Yi Zhong Chu Zi [2002] No. 1619) of the First Intermediate People's Court of Beijing. The Criminal Judgment (Yi Zhong Chu Zi [2002] No. 1619) of the First Intermediate People's Court of Beijing ultimately found that Fang Zeping, the acting general manager of Hongye Company, constituted the crime of letter of credit fraud. However, the crimes and criminal facts found in that judgment have no direct connection with the guarantee dispute in this case.

This court, upon trial, finds: This case is a dispute over a guarantee contract. The guarantee in question is a guarantee provided by a domestic company as the guarantor for foreign currency loans of a Hong Kong company. This guarantee is an external guarantee. Although the parties agreed in the guarantee deed to apply Hong Kong law, since the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the mainland of China belong to different legal jurisdictions, according to the principle established in Article 194 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, when choosing the applicable law in foreign-related contracts, the parties may not evade the mandatory or prohibitive legal norms of China. The mainland of China has mandatory provisions regarding external guarantees. If the guarantee deed in this case applies Hong Kong law, it would clearly evade the above mandatory provisions. Therefore, the agreement of the parties in this case regarding the application of Hong Kong law to the guarantee deed has no legal effect. This dispute shall be governed by the laws of the mainland of China as the lex causae.

This case is currently only a trial of the guarantee contract dispute. The principal debtor under the main contract to which the guarantee contract relates, Hong Kong Dalifeng Group Limited, has already been wound up and dissolved. On January 3, 2000, the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, in Companies Winding-up Case No. 883 of 1999, confirmed the creditor's rights of Guohua Bank against Dalifeng Group Limited to be a total of principal HKD 44,082,157.07 and USD 25,771,093.15, together with interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61. On May 22 of the same year, the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Limited, lawyer Yiu Leung Keung of Ernst & Young, Hong Kong, by letter file reference NC/PY/DC/st/0005-L10953, confirmed Guohua Bank's claim against Dalifeng Group Limited as principal of HKD 44,082,157.07 and USD 25,771,093.15, and interest of HKD 1,443,383.13 and USD 708,517.61. During the proceedings of this court, the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Limited again confirmed the above debt amounts. Hongye Company appealed, arguing that it enjoys the right to raise defenses of the principal debtor, including but not limited to defenses against the authenticity of the amount of the creditor's rights, and that the court of first instance should not have used the creditor's rights declared by Guohua Bank to the Official Receiver's Office as the evidence of the creditor's rights in this case. This court finds that Hongye Company does indeed enjoy such a right of defense. However, Hongye Company failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that the principal debt amount confirmed by the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Limited, appointed by the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, was false or inaccurate. Therefore, this court confirms the principal debt amount as confirmed by the liquidator of Dalifeng Group Limited. The interest on the above principal debts was calculated up to January 3, 2000. In expressing the liability to be borne by Hongye Company and Xinye Company, the judgment of the court of first instance additionally calculated interest on the above principal debts from January 4, 2000 until the date of full payment. However, Guohua Bank did not claim interest after January 4, 2000 in its complaint. During the second instance of this court, Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited also did not claim interest after January 4, 2000. Therefore, this court will not consider interest after January 4, 2000.

In this case, Hongye Company issued an "Irrevocable Guarantee Contract" to Guohua Bank. This guarantee contract was affixed with the company's seal, and during the second instance trial of this court, Hongye Company explicitly stated that it had no objection to the authenticity of the company seal. Hongye Company claimed that this guarantee contract was forged by Fang Zeping, the then acting general manager of the company, but it failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove this. Although Hongye Company submitted a criminal judgment from a people's court to prove that Fang Zeping had engaged in criminal conduct, that judgment found Fang Zeping guilty of letter of credit fraud, and the criminal conduct described therein is not directly related to this case. Therefore, this court does not support its appellate request to transfer this case to the public security authority for prior handling. Article 23, paragraph 1, of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a third party unilaterally issues a guarantee document in writing to a creditor, and the creditor accepts it without raising any objection, the guarantee contract is established." Since Hongye Company provided an "Irrevocable Guarantee Contract" bearing its genuine company seal to Guohua Bank, and that "Irrevocable Guarantee Contract" was accepted by Guohua Bank without objection, based on the above facts and provisions, it should be determined that the guarantee contract between Guohua Bank and Hongye Company has been established.

Hongye Company argued that the affixing of the seal on the guarantee contract in this case constituted an act of ultra vires, and that Guohua Bank should have known of this, therefore the guarantee contract should have no legal effect on Guohua Bank. Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a legal representative or responsible person of a legal person or other organization enters into a guarantee contract beyond its authority, the act of representation shall be valid, except where the counterparty knew or should have known of the ultra vires act." Hongye Company failed to provide evidence to prove that Guohua Bank knew or should have known, at the time it obtained the guarantee contract, that the guarantee contract was entered into by its legal representative beyond authority. When Guohua Bank obtained the guarantee contract from Hongye Company, it also obtained a board resolution bearing the genuine seal of Hongye Company, which indicated that the guarantee act of Hongye Company had been approved by the board of directors. Although this court, after trial, ultimately refused to confirm the authenticity of the contents of the "Board of Directors Meeting Resolution," Hongye Company only raised objections to the authenticity of the "Board of Directors Meeting Resolution" after the dispute in this case arose, and it could not provide sufficient evidence to prove that Guohua Bank knew or should have known, at the time it obtained the guarantee contract, that the guarantee contract was signed ultra vires. On the contrary, the fact that Guohua Bank obtained the board resolution bearing the genuine seal of Hongye Company precisely indicates that Guohua Bank had ample reason at that time to believe that the guarantee contract issued by Hongye Company had been approved by its board of directors and that there was no ultra vires act. Therefore, Hongye Company's appellate argument that the affixing of the seal on the guarantee contract in this case constituted an ultra vires act and that the guarantee contract should have no legal effect on Guohua Bank cannot be established.

In the first and second instances of this case, Xinye Company, after being lawfully summoned, did not appear in court to respond to the action without justifiable reasons. Xinye Company did not raise any objection to the guarantee contract and board resolution issued by Xinye Company that were provided by Guohua Bank. The court of first instance correctly determined that the guarantee issued by Xinye Company was its true intention and was lawfully established.

Hongye Company and Xinye Company provided guarantees for foreign currency borrowings by Hong Kong companies from Hong Kong banks; such guarantees constitute external guarantees. According to the relevant regulations of mainland China regarding external guarantees, such guarantees should be registered and approved by the foreign exchange control authorities. However, the guarantee contracts issued by Hongye Company and Xinye Company in this case did not undergo the above procedures. Pursuant to Article 6, Item (1), of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, these guarantee contracts should be determined to be invalid. The court of first instance correctly determined the validity of the guarantee contracts in this case. However, the court of first instance held that the responsibility for the invalidity of the guarantee contracts fell entirely on Hongye Company and Xinye Company, which constitutes an improper allocation of responsibility. The creditor, Guohua Bank, also bears fault for causing the invalidity of the guarantee contracts. As a creditor, Guohua Bank, when accepting the guarantees, had an obligation to ascertain whether the guarantors, Hongye Company and Xinye Company, were qualified to issue such guarantees, whether such guarantees required approval from the relevant authorities, and whether the guarantors had fulfilled the approval procedures. If the relevant guarantee procedures were incomplete, Guohua Bank had an obligation to urge the guarantors to remedy them, thereby obtaining a complete and effective guarantee to better protect its own rights and interests. However, in this case, where the guarantees issued by Hongye Company and Xinye Company had not been approved and registered by the relevant foreign exchange control authorities, Guohua Bank failed to fulfill its aforementioned obligations and accepted them. Therefore, with respect to the invalidity of the two guarantee contracts involved in this case due to the lack of statutory approval and registration procedures, Hongye Company, Xinye Company, and Guohua Bank all bear fault. This court supports Hongye Company's appellate request that Guohua Bank bears fault for causing the invalidity of the guarantee contracts. The court of first instance improperly allocated responsibility by holding that the responsibility for the invalidity of the guarantee contracts fell entirely on the guarantors, Hongye Company and Xinye Company, and this court should correct this. Pursuant to Article 61, paragraph 1, of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5, paragraph 2, of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall each bear corresponding compensatory liability for the portion of the principal debtor's obligations that cannot be satisfied. Even if Hongye Company and Xinye Company undertook to bear all responsibility if the guarantees were invalid due to failure to go through the procedures required by law, such undertaking should be determined to be invalid. As stated above, with respect to the invalidity of the guarantee contracts, Hongye Company, Xinye Company, and the creditor Guohua Bank all bear fault. According to relevant legal provisions, Hongye Company and Xinye Company shall only bear corresponding compensatory liability for the portion of the principal debtor's obligations that cannot be satisfied. If the undertaking of Hongye Company and Xinye Company to bear all responsibility were to be held valid, it would not only violate the above provisions but also circumvent the relevant regulations of our country on foreign exchange control. It would allow the creditor, in a situation where an external guarantee contract is invalid due to lack of approval and registration by our country's foreign exchange control authorities, to obtain the same result as if the guarantee contract were valid. Therefore, the above undertakings of Hongye Company and Xinye Company should be determined to be invalid. Although Xinye Company did not appeal, according to Article 35 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Reforming the Methods of Civil and Economic Trial, this court should also correct the improper allocation of responsibility in the judgment of the first instance.

Furthermore, although Hongye Company appealed, claiming that the procedure of the first instance was seriously unlawful and requested that the case be remanded for retrial, it failed to provide specific facts and reasons in its notice of appeal to prove the existence of statutory circumstances warranting a remand. This court does not support Hongye Company's appellate request for a remand.

In summary, except for the erroneous determination of the authenticity of the "Board of Directors Meeting Resolution" issued by Hongye Company, the court of first instance correctly found the other facts. However, the allocation of responsibility for Hongye Company and Xinye Company was improper, and this court corrects it. In addition, due to the merger and change of Guohua Bank, the rights and obligations formerly held by the original Guohua Bank in this case are now enjoyed and borne by Bank of China (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 61, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5, paragraph 2 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 194 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 6, Item (1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, this court now renders judgment as follows:

1. The civil judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court, (2000) Yue Fa Jing Er Chu Zi No. 5, is set aside.
